newsitem.title: UK: Vitec upbeat despite sterling strength.
newsitem.headline: Vitec upbeat despite sterling strength.

text.p: Vitec Group Plc said on Friday that it was well protected against the strength of sterling and was upbeat about future prospects.
The company, which supplies broadcast and photographic equipment and derives around 90 percent of its profits from overseas, lifted pretax profits for 1996 to 52.6 million stg from 30.7 previously.
Profits were boosted by an exceptional profit of 16 million on the sale of its unit W Vinten Ltd in September 1996.

"The markets which the group serves continue to be robust and, despite the adverse effect of the strength of sterling on the reporting of overseas profits, we look forward to 1997 with confidence," said Malcolm Baggott, chief executive of Vitec.

Sterling has steadily climbed through 1996 and into 1997, squeezing profits on British companies with overseas earnings once they are translated back into sterling. It had strengthened to around 2.76 marks by February of this year having started 1996 at around 2.43 marks.
Vitec said that the combined impact of transaction and translation differences in 1996 from 1995 reduced profits by around 1.9 million, stg, but was offset by profits of hedging of 1.6 million.
It noted that if the exchange rates at the end of February 1997 had prevailed in 1996 then reported profits, before hedging, would have been around four percent lower.
The company increased its total dividend payout by 15 percent to 12.1p.
Shares in the firm had risen 14-1/2p to stand at 652-1/2 by 0835 GMT.
